extracted.intended_audience: professional journalists, newsroom editors, journalism educators and students
extracted.subtask_description: A professional code setting ethical standards and practical guidelines for journalists across media and specialties, covering truthfulness, minimizing harm, independence, and accountability in news gathering and reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preamble
rubrics_metrics.description: Members of the Society of Professional Journalists believe that public enlightenment is the forerunner of justice and the foundation of democracy. The duty of the journalist is to further those ends by seeking truth and providing a fair and comprehensive account of events and issues. Conscientious journalists from all media and specialties strive to serve the public with thoroughness and honesty. Professional integrity is the cornerstone of a journalist's credibility. Members of the Society share a dedication to ethical behavior and adopt this code to declare the Society's principles and standards of practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets the overarching purpose: public enlightenment, seeking truth, fairness, thoroughness, honesty, and professional integrity as the foundation for all other guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voluntary nature of the Code
rubrics_metrics.description: The SPJ Code of Ethics is voluntarily embraced by thousands of journalists, regardless of place or platform, and is widely used in newsrooms and classrooms as a guide for ethical behavior. The code is intended not as a set of 'rules' but as a resource for ethical decision-making. It is not — nor can it be under the First Amendment — legally enforceable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The code should be used as advisory guidance and a decision-making resource rather than a legal standard; promotes discussion and judgement rather than rigid enforcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Test accuracy and avoid error
rubrics_metrics.description: Test the accuracy of information from all sources and exercise care to avoid inadvertent error. Deliberate distortion is never permissible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fact-check information from all sources; make all reasonable efforts to verify; avoid both inadvertent mistakes and deliberate distortion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seek response from subjects
rubrics_metrics.description: Diligently seek out subjects of news stories to give them the opportunity to respond to allegations of wrongdoing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make good-faith efforts to contact and include responses from people accused or implicated before publishing allegations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify sources whenever feasible
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify sources whenever feasible. The public is entitled to as much information as possible on sources' reliability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer named sources; when anonymity is used, explain the reliability and context to the audience where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Question motives before granting anonymity; keep promises
rubrics_metrics.description: Always question sources' motives before promising anonymity. Clarify conditions attached to any promise made in exchange for information. Keep promises.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess why a source wants anonymity, document agreed conditions, and honor confidentiality commitments unless overridden by overriding ethical considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid misrepresentation in presentation and promos
rubrics_metrics.description: Make certain that headlines, news teases and promotional material, photos, video, audio, graphics, sound bites and quotations do not misrepresent. They should not oversimplify or highlight incidents out of context.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure all presentation elements accurately reflect the story's substance and context to avoid misleading audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not distort news photos or video; label edits
rubrics_metrics.description: Never distort the content of news photos or video. Image enhancement for technical clarity is always permissible. Label montages and photo illustrations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permitted: technical clarity enhancements. Prohibited: altering images in ways that change meaning. Always disclose montages, illustrations, or significant edits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid misleading re-enactments; label if used
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid misleading re-enactments or staged news events. If re-enactment is necessary to tell a story, label it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not present staged or re-created scenes as if they were original footage; clearly label re-enactments to readers/viewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use undercover/surreptitious methods only when vital
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid undercover or other surreptitious methods of gathering information except when traditional open methods will not yield information vital to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If such methods are used, explain their use and necessity as part of the story to justify the intrusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Never plagiarize
rubrics_metrics.description: Never plagiarize.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Always attribute and credit others' words and work; do not present others' material as your own under any circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tell diverse human stories boldly
rubrics_metrics.description: Tell the story of the diversity and magnitude of the human experience boldly, even when it is unpopular to do so.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strive for inclusive coverage that reflects different communities and experiences, resisting pressure to avoid controversial perspectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examine and avoid imposing cultural values
rubrics_metrics.description: Examine their own cultural values and avoid imposing those values on others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be self-aware about biases; avoid editorializing from cultural assumptions when reporting on people or communities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid stereotyping
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid stereotyping by race, gender, age, religion, ethnicity, geography, sexual orientation, disability, physical appearance or social status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose language and frames that do not reduce individuals or groups to stereotypes; seek nuance and complexity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support open exchange of views
rubrics_metrics.description: Support the open exchange of views, even views they find repugnant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cover a range of perspectives and protect the principle of free expression while providing accurate context and analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Give voice to the voiceless
rubrics_metrics.description: Give voice to the voiceless; official and unofficial sources of information can be equally valid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include perspectives from marginalized and less-heard voices as part of comprehensive reporting, assessing credibility appropriately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish advocacy from news reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinguish between advocacy and news reporting. Analysis and commentary should be labeled and not misrepresent fact or context.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Label opinion, analysis, and commentary clearly; avoid mixing advocacy with factual reporting in ways that mislead audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish news from advertising
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinguish news from advertising and shun hybrids that blur the lines between the two.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid native ads or sponsored content presented as editorial; disclose paid content and maintain separation between editorial and commercial interests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure public business is conducted in the open
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize a special obligation to ensure that the public's business is conducted in the open and that government records are open to inspection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize reporting that exposes public business and use freedom of information tools to obtain government records.

rubrics_metrics.name: Show compassion; special sensitivity for children/inexperienced sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Show compassion for those who may be affected adversely by news coverage. Use special sensitivity when dealing with children and inexperienced sources or subjects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply extra care, consent practices, and protective measures when interviewing or photographing vulnerable people.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be sensitive when seeking/using interviews or photos of tragedy victims
rubrics_metrics.description: Be sensitive when seeking or using interviews or photographs of those affected by tragedy or grief.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Weigh news value against potential harm; avoid intrusive or sensational treatment of victims and grieving families.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognize reporting may cause harm; avoid arrogance
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize that gathering and reporting information may cause harm or discomfort. Pursuit of the news is not a license for arrogance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance public interest with potential harm; do not use authority of journalism as excuse to demean or exploit sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respect privacy of private individuals
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize that private people have a greater right to control information about themselves than do public officials and others who seek power, influence or attention. Only an overriding public need can justify intrusion into anyone’s privacy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Differentiate public figures from private individuals and justify intrusions only when a clear and overriding public interest exists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Show good taste; avoid pandering to lurid curiosity
rubrics_metrics.description: Show good taste. Avoid pandering to lurid curiosity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refrain from sensationalism and gratuitous detail that serve prurient interest rather than public understanding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be cautious identifying juveniles and sex-crime victims
rubrics_metrics.description: Be cautious about identifying juvenile suspects or victims of sex crimes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protect identities of minors and sensitive victims unless there is compelling public-interest justification for naming them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be judicious naming criminal suspects before charges
rubrics_metrics.description: Be judicious about naming criminal suspects before the formal filing of charges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid prematurely naming suspects where doing so could cause undue harm or mislead the public; consider legal and ethical implications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance fair trial rights with public's right to know
rubrics_metrics.description: Balance a criminal suspect's fair trial rights with the public's right to be informed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider how coverage might prejudice legal proceedings and weigh that risk against the necessity of public disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid conflicts of interest, real or perceived
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid conflicts of interest, real or perceived.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refrain from activities or relationships that could compromise objectivity or create the appearance of bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remain free of compromising associations or activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Remain free of associations and activities that may compromise integrity or damage credibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess outside affiliations, memberships, or roles that could undermine perceived neutrality; recuse or disclose when necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refuse gifts/favors and avoid compromising employment/roles
rubrics_metrics.description: Refuse gifts, favors, fees, free travel and special treatment, and shun secondary employment, political involvement, public office and service in community organizations if they compromise journalistic integrity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid accepting benefits that might influence coverage; consider institutional policies on gifts and travel; avoid roles that conflict with journalistic duties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclose unavoidable conflicts
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclose unavoidable conflicts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When conflicts cannot be avoided, be transparent with editors and audiences about their nature and possible effects on coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hold those with power accountable
rubrics_metrics.description: Be vigilant and courageous about holding those with power accountable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pursue investigative reporting and oversight without fear or favoritism; follow evidence and public-interest motives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deny favored treatment to advertisers and special interests
rubrics_metrics.description: Deny favored treatment to advertisers and special interests and resist their pressure to influence news coverage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain editorial independence from commercial pressures; establish and enforce firewall policies between ad sales and newsroom.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be wary of sources offering information for favors or money
rubrics_metrics.description: Be wary of sources offering information for favors or money; avoid bidding for news.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not pay sources for news or engage in transactions that could bias or compromise reporting; verify motives of paid informants carefully.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarify coverage and invite public dialogue
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarify and explain news coverage and invite dialogue with the public over journalistic conduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide behind-the-scenes explanations where appropriate, make editorial decisions transparent, and welcome audience questions and corrections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encourage public grievances
rubrics_metrics.description: Encourage the public to voice grievances against the news media.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide accessible channels for complaints and feedback and treat them seriously.

rubrics_metrics.name: Admit mistakes and correct promptly
rubrics_metrics.description: Admit mistakes and correct them promptly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acknowledge errors publicly, correct the record quickly and visibly, and explain what went wrong and how future mistakes will be prevented.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expose unethical practices in journalism
rubrics_metrics.description: Expose unethical practices of journalists and the news media.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigate and report on misconduct within the profession; apply the same standards to peers as to others.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abide by same high standards held for others
rubrics_metrics.description: Abide by the same high standards to which they hold others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practice self-scrutiny and apply ethical standards consistently to one's own work and behavior.
